verdict.rationale: Neon documents isolated database branches as its sandbox mechanism: agents run migrations and query optimizations on temporary branches while production stays untouched. Each branch also gets its own isolated auth environment, and neon.ts can set TTLs so branches auto-expire. A hands-on community user confirms branching off main to test and then resetting the branch to its parent, so this is true isolation, not a dry-run. Missing for 10: detailed first-party evidence of branch isolation semantics (the branching docs page appears only as a title in the pack).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: run safe schema migrations and query optimizations on temporary Neon branches, keeping production untouched until changes are validated
Every database branch gets its own isolated auth environment, so you can test sign-up, login, and OAuth flows in preview or CI branches without touching production.
We can branch off the main database to test things out, and periodically reset the branch to its parent.
